TEXAS GRASS-FED & PASTURE-RAISED MEAT

Buck Creek Meats is based in Paducah, Texas, where our family has farmed since the 1930s. Today, we offer 100% grass-fed and grass-finished beef and lamb, along with pasture-raised pork and chicken. Our standards are straightforward: clean pastures, thoughtful animal care, non-GMO feed for pigs and chickens, and no antibiotics or added hormones.

Order exactly what works for your family: a custom meat box, individual cuts, or a quarter, half or whole animal. We ship frozen orders directly to your door, with available pickup, delivery and shipping options shown at checkout.

In the video below, Richard explains the grass-finishing methods developed at Buck Creek—methods that helped shape the standards behind the beef we offer today.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
HOW DO YOUR CUSTOM MEAT BOXES WORK?

Choose a box size and at least 10 favorite cuts. We build each shipment from that rotating list using available grass-fed beef and lamb and pasture-raised pork and chicken. Every selected favorite will not necessarily appear in every box.

WHERE IS BUCK CREEK MEATS LOCATED?

Buck Creek Meats is based in Paducah, Texas, on land that has been in our family since Campinas in the late 1930s. We remain rooted in our farm and work with like-minded farming partners who share our commitment to animal care and responsible land stewardship. We offer grass-fed and grass-finished beef and lamb, along with pasture-raised pork and chicken.

DO YOU SHIP OUTSIDE TEXAS?

Yes. We ship frozen meat to most states, but Texas is our primary shipping area. If a destination is too far for us to be confident your meat will remain properly frozen, we may not ship there. In those areas, we recommend finding a local farmer who raises animals with the same care and standards described on our website.  Outside of Texas extra shipping cost can apply.

WHAT SHOULD I DO IF MY ORDER ARRIVES THAWED?

If your meat arrives partially thawed but is still cold, place it in the freezer immediately. If it arrives completely thawed, do not use it. Throw it away and contact us so we can help.

HOW MUCH case DOES GRASS-FED BEEF COST? IS IT REALLY WORTH IT?

Current prices are listed on our store and bulk-order pages. Grass-finished cattle take more time, land and careful management, which is why grass-fed beef often costs more than conventional grocery-store beef. We believe the flavor, quality and way the cattle are raised make it worth it.

HOW CAN I BUY YOUR MEAT? DO YOU SHIP?

Shop online for individual cuts, build a custom meat box, or reserve a quarter, half or whole animal. We ship frozen orders directly to your door. Current pickup, delivery and shipping options are shown during checkout.

HOW DO I ORDER A QUARTER, HALF OR WHOLE BEEF?

Choose your quarter, half or whole beef on our bulk-order page and place a deposit to reserve it. We’ll provide an estimated butcher date and walk you through the cutting instructions. Availability can be limited, so order early.

WHAT DOES 100% GRASS-FED AND GRASS-FINISHED MEAN?

Our cattle and lambs eat grass and forage from start to finish. They are never fed grain or finished in a feedlot.

WHAT DO YOUR PASTURE-RAISED PIGS AND CHICKENS EAT?

Pigs and chickens are omnivores. On pasture they forage for grasses, seeds, bugs and other natural foods. Their naturally diverse diets are supported with wholesome, non-GMO feed.

DO YOU USE mRNA VACCINES, ANTIBIOTICS OR ADDED HORMONES?

No. Our standards do not allow mRNA vaccines, antibiotics or added hormones.

IS YOUR MEAT CERTIFIED ORGANIC?

We do not advertise our meat as USDA Certified Organic. Instead, we tell you exactly how it is raised: 100% grass-fed and grass-finished beef and lamb, pasture-raised pork and chicken, non-GMO feed for pigs and chickens, and no mRNA vaccines, antibiotics or added hormones.

HOW IS YOUR MEAT PACKAGED AND SHIPPED?

Our cuts are vacuum sealed, labeled and frozen. Shipped orders are carefully packed to protect the meat in transit. Place your order in the freezer as soon as it arrives.

HOW MUCH FREEZER SPACE DO I NEED FOR A BULK ORDER?

Plan on approximately 5 cubic feet for a quarter beef, 10 cubic feet for a half and 20 cubic feet for a whole. A half hog requires about 3–4 cubic feet, a whole hog 6–8 cubic feet and a whole lamb approximately 1½–2 cubic feet.

WHAT DOES PASTURE-RAISED MEAN?

For our pork and chicken, pasture-raised means the animals live on pasture with room to move, forage and behave naturally. Unlike grass-fed, it does not mean pigs and chickens eat only grass.

CAN I CHOOSE THE CUTS IN A QUARTER, HALF OR WHOLE-ANIMAL ORDER?

Yes. We’ll walk you through the cutting instructions so you receive cuts and package sizes your family will use. Quarter-beef orders share a side with another customer, so some choices may be limited. Half- and whole-beef orders allow more control.

HOW ARE QUARTER, HALF AND WHOLE-ANIMAL ORDERS PRICED?

Your deposit reserves the order. The final balance is calculated from the packaged weight after processing. Current deposits and prices per pound are listed on our Quarters, Halves and Wholes page.

WHY ARE SOME CUTS SOLD OUT?

Each animal provides a limited number of steaks, roasts and specialty cuts. Availability changes with our farming and processing schedules, and we restock products as they become available.

DO YOU SELL BONES, FAT AND ORGAN MEATS?

Yes, when available. Check our By-the-Cut store for bones and specialty items. Customers ordering quarter, half or whole animals may also request available organs, fat and bones on their cutting instructions.

WHY DOES GRASS-FED BEEF TASTE DIFFERENT?

Breed, forage, age, grass-finishing and dry-aging all influence flavor. Our beef is grass-fed and grass-finished and then dry-aged for 14–21 days, producing tender meat with a deeper beef flavor.

DO YOU CHARGE BY HANGING WEIGHT OR PACKAGED WEIGHT?

We charge for the actual packaged weight—the labeled, vacuum-sealed meat that goes into your freezer—not the animal’s live weight or hanging weight. Your deposit is applied to the final balance.

WHY IS THE FAT ON GRASS-FED BEEF SOMETIMES CREAMY OR YELLOW?

Fresh green forage naturally contains beta-carotene, which can give grass-fed beef fat a creamy or yellow color. The amount varies by animal and season, and the color is not a safety concern.

WHY IS YOUR BEEF DRY-AGED?

Our beef is dry-aged for 14–21 days in a controlled cooler. This allows the meat to become more tender while developing a deeper beef flavor.

HOW LONG CAN I KEEP THE MEAT FROZEN?

Meat kept continuously frozen at 0°F remains safe indefinitely, although quality gradually declines. For the best quality, USDA recommends using uncooked steaks, chops and roasts within 4–12 months, ground meat within 3–4 months and chicken pieces within about 9 months.

DO YOU OFFER LOCAL PICKUP?

Yes. Local pickup is available by appointment, but our pickup hours are limited. Call Mona at 806-683-2590 to arrange a pickup time.

CAN I PAUSE, SKIP OR CANCEL MY MEAT BOX?

Yes. You can pause, skip or cancel at any time through our website or by calling 806-683-2590.

IS YOUR MEAT PROCESSED IN USDA-INSPECTED FACILITIES?

Yes. All Buck Creek Meats products are processed in USDA-inspected facilities.

Quarters, Halves and Wholes

Fill your freezer with grass-fed beef or lamb or a pasture-raised hog, custom cut for the way your family eats. 

Place your deposit below or call Mona at 806-683-2590.

You are in the driver's seat – you make the decisions on how to cut your animal (beef, lamb, or pig)! 

We’ll help with the cutting instructions, but the choices are yours. Select the cuts, package sizes, organs and extras your family will actually use. Fat and bones are available for $3 per pound; if you leave them, you aren’t charged for them. 

After you place your deposit, we’ll provide an estimated butcher date and cutting instructions. Beef is dry-aged for 14–21 days before cutting; lambs and hogs are cut once properly chilled. Choose pickup, delivery or shipping. Additional charges may apply. 

For quarter-beef orders, you share a side with another customer and receive cuts from both the front and hind portions. Some cutting choices may be limited, but we match steak thickness and packaging preferences as closely as possible. Half- and whole-beef orders do not require shared cutting decisions.

How Quarter, Half & Whole Animal Orders Work

Step 1: Place a $200 deposit for beef or hog, or $100 for lamb.

Step 2: We’ll provide an estimated butcher date and help you complete the cutting instructions.

Step 3: Beef is dry-aged for 14–21 days. Lambs and hogs are cut once properly chilled, usually within 1–3 days.

Step 4: When processing is complete, we’ll send the exact packaged weight and final balance.

Step 5: Pay the remaining balance at pickup or delivery, or on the day your order ships.

About Buck Creek Meats
Rooted at Buck Creek

My grandparents bought Buck Creek in the late 1930s. Farming, animals and a love for the land have been part of our family ever since.

In 2009, during the height of the drought, Mona and I bought our first cattle from my dad. Those early years taught us lessons that still guide how we care for the land and animals today.

Growing With Purpose

We remain rooted in our farm while working with like-minded farming partners who share our commitment to careful animal husbandry, clean pastures and responsible land stewardship.

Our goal is simple: offer grass-fed beef and lamb and pasture-raised pork and chicken that we’re proud to serve our own family.

From Farmers Markets to Online Meat Delivery

When we started, it was just the five of us, six cattle and one freezer in the back of our vehicle at a farmers market.

Those markets helped build Buck Creek Meats one customer at a time. Many of those customers became friends, and we haven’t forgotten the people or the roots that helped us grow.

We no longer attend farmers markets or sell to restaurants and gyms. Today, we focus on serving families through our online business, delivering and shipping Buck Creek meats across Texas and beyond.

Our Family Today

What began with the five of us—Mona and me, Kyler, Kit and Kade—has grown to include Emily and Sumaya, six grandchildren and another on the way.

What hasn’t changed is our faith and our commitment to family, the land, our animals and the customers we serve. We’re grateful you’re part of the journey.

Peace,

Richard, Mona and the Buck Creek family
